prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, system, budget and whether you need an emergency repair or a replacement. I can help you find a highly‑rated local tech, but first a few quick tips so you can choose the best company in Phoenix for your situation.

What to look for
- Valid Arizona contractor license (ROC) and liability insurance — ask for the ROC number and verify it.  
- NATE‑certified technicians (or equivalent training) and experience with your make/model.  
- Clear, written diagnostic/repair estimate (including parts, labor, taxes, fees).  
- Warranty on parts and labor (get length and coverage in writing).  
- 24/7 emergency service if you need fast response in extreme heat.  
- Good current reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi and an acceptable BBB rating.  
- Willingness to pull permits and follow local code for replacements.  
- Transparent pricing (no high‑pressure “must replace” sales tactics).  

Red flags
- No ROC/license or won’t provide it.  
- Only accepts cash and won’t give a written receipt.  
- Very low price compared to everyone else with no clear explanation.  
- Repeated poor reviews mentioning no‑shows, upselling, or shoddy workmanship.

Practical rules of thumb
- If your unit is older than ~10–15 years or a repair will cost more than ~50% of replacement cost, replacement is often the better value.  
- If your system uses R‑22 refrigerant (older units), recharge costs can be very high — consider replacement.  
- Ask for a written estimate for both repair and a replacement option so you can compare apples to apples.

If you want, I can find top-rated HVAC companies near you in Phoenix. Tell me:
- ZIP code or neighborhood, and  
- Whether this is an emergency repair or a planned replacement, and  
- System brand/model and symptoms (won’t cool, leaking, noisy, tripping breaker, etc.)

With that I’ll pull a short list of well-reviewed local contractors, summarize their strengths, and what to ask each when you call.
